artworks.title: La Muse malade
artworks.medium: lithograph in brown on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a woman and various ghostly figures. The drawing shows a nude figure alongside shadowy creatures. A spectral female figure is in the foreground with long hair. Alongside her are an eerie bird-like creature and a skull-like face. The title "La Muse Malade" is written above in stylized letters, translating to "The Sick Muse." At the bottom right is a simple line drawing of a stringed instrument. The piece features minimal lines and soft tones, giving it an ethereal and haunting quality.

artworks.title: La Fumée, puis la flamme
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring an ethereal scene of smoke turning into flames with swirling patterns. The smoke starts from the bottom left and transforms into sweeping flame-like shapes towards the top right. A figure reaches into the flames. The colors transition from navy to orange and yellow. Text on the right side provides details about a theatrical production, potentially a play titled "La Fumée, puis la Flamme" at Le Théâtre Libre during the 1895-1896 season. The artwork reflects elements of Art Nouveau with its flowing lines and organic forms.

artworks.title: Père
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of an advertisement poster for a theatrical performance. The image showcases a vintage theatre poster, primarily focused on promoting a "Soirée de Gala" at the Théâtre de l'Œuvre. The poster is illustrated in monochromatic tones with a dominant use of black and white. The left side features extensive text detailing the event, including the title "PÈRE" by August Strindberg, along with a list of cast members. On the right, an illustrated scene depicts two figures, one of whom appears to be writing or reading at a table, while another figure looks on. The background is filled with additional decorative and promotional text related to the editions and distribution of the play.

artworks.title: Le Cloître (The Cloister)
artworks.medium: lithograph printed in yellow-brown on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural scene with arches. The image depicts a minimalist portrayal of an ancient or medieval architectural setting, featuring grand arches and columns. The pale, monochromatic, and light sepia tones give it an aged look. There are silhouetted figures in the image, enhancing the religious or monastic atmosphere suggested by the title "Le Cloître". The text on the image indicates its connection to a theater production.

artworks.title: Le Joug
artworks.medium: lithograph in green on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatrical play's cover design. The artwork depicts an unclothed figure pulling a heavy apparatus. The illustration creates a contrast between light and shadow, giving a dramatic effect. The background is textured and shaded, suggesting an industrial or oppressive environment. The title "LE JOUG" is featured prominently on the right side, along with credits for the play, character names, and associated personnel. The drawing's lines and shading emphasize the physical strain depicted, conveying a sense of struggle and burden.

artworks.title: Le Cuivre
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on pink wove paper
artworks.description: The image is a vintage theatrical poster featuring a woman's body from the torso to above the knees. The woman is reclining with her head tilted slightly backward. Her face is not clearly visible, and she wears an ornament or jewelry on her head. She has long hair blending into the dark background. She wears a long dress with a floral pattern, a prominent neckline, and sleeves covering her arms. The background fades from a light hue at the center to a darker setting at the edges. The poster includes text on the left side detailing a theatrical production titled "Le Cuivre" associated with Le Théâtre Libre Saison in 1895-1896.

artworks.title: Le Cuivre
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on pink wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows an illustration of a woman in a darkened environment. The woman is depicted leaning on a railing or barrier, with the text in French in the background indicating a theatrical production related to "Le Cuivre" during the 1895-1896 season by Le Théâtre Libre.

artworks.title: Ames solitaires
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a vintage advertisement or magazine cover with text and abstract human figures in a sepia-toned drawing. The left side includes the words "paraîtra à partir du 1er Janvier 1894 la Revue blanche Transformée." The right side features the text "ames Solitaires de Gerhart Hauptmann." The background shows abstract shapes and two human figures engaged in activities near writings and artistic flourishes.

artworks.title: Au-delà des forces humaines
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows a vertically oriented artwork combining illustration and text. The scene depicts a rural landscape, with dense vertical brushstrokes resembling tree trunks on the left side. In the background, there are buildings and curved lines suggesting a countryside setting. The style features rough brushstrokes in dark and light tones on a sepia background, giving the impression of movement and texture. A rectangular block of text on the left side details a theatrical piece titled "Au delà des Forces," including cast and venue information.

artworks.title: Au dessus des forces humaines; L'Araignée de cristal
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of an artistic promotional poster. The image is split into two sections, each filled with dynamic illustrations and text. The left side features figures with the repeated phrase "Lisez la Review Blanche." The right side shows a gathering of people in a potentially indoor setting, with text listing details about an event at "Bouffes du Nord." The text is written in an expressive style that matches the energy of the figures.

artworks.title: Frères; La Gardienne; Créanciers
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a poster or advertisement for a performance. It features a variety of sketches and text describing different performances, likely in French. The top section includes abstract tree and foliage sketches alongside inverted text. The middle section lists names of performances and performers' roles. The bottom section provides details about the venue and event, potentially at "Salle de la Comédie Parisienne." The design showcases intricate typography and illustrative elements inspired by late 19th or early 20th century European art nouveau style.

artworks.title: Monsieur Bute; L'Amant de sa femme; La Belle opération
artworks.medium: photo-relief with watercolor stenciling (pochoir print) on wove paper
artworks.dimensions:
sheet (program closed): 21.5 x 19.9 cm (8 7/16 x 7 13/16 in.)
sheet (program opened): 21.5 x 39.6 cm (8 7/16 x 15 9/16 in.)
artworks.description: This is an illustration of a figure in a light green outfit next to a tree. The figure is bent over with hands touching the ground and the top of their head visible. A tree is on the left, and the background shows foliage sketches. On the right, "THEATRE LIBRE" is written vertically. The style is reminiscent of early modern or post-impressionist art, with thick outlines and subtle coloration.

artworks.title: The Bathers (Small Plate)
artworks.medium: color lithograph on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Frank R. and Jeannette H. Eyerly
artworks.description: This is a painting of multiple nude figures in a natural setting. The scene shows the figures lounging and standing near the water's edge in a serene environment. The figures are depicted with soft lines, gentle shading, and a relaxed sense of movement and interaction. The background includes trees and foliage with brushstrokes indicating a lush atmosphere. The color palette consists of soft shades of blue, green, and earthy tones, contributing to the tranquil mood of the painting. The style is reminiscent of Paul Cézanne, known for his exploration of the human form and integration of landscape.

artworks.title: Wendingen
artworks.medium: color lithograph; cover for the illustrated magazine "Wendingen" [plus the 36-page text]
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Frank R. and Jeannette H. Eyerly

artworks.title: A Peasant Woman Goes for Water
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Frank R. and Jeannette H. Eyerly
artworks.description: The image depicts a complex arrangement of geometric shapes and angular lines. Triangles, rectangles, and shaded areas interlock to create an abstract composition with a patchwork-like appearance. There are forms that resemble figures or structures found in urban landscapes. The drawing consists of sharp edges and varying shades of gray. The interplay of shapes suggests movement and interaction, prompting viewers to examine how these forms align into recognizable patterns.

artworks.title: Standing Philosopher and Two Other Figures
artworks.medium: etching on laid paper
artworks.dimensions:
plate: 13.3 x 17.2 cm (5 1/4 x 6 3/4 in.)
sheet (trimmed close to plate mark): 13.6 x 17.5 cm (5 3/8 x 6 7/8 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Frank R. and Jeannette H. Eyerly
artworks.description: The image shows two figures from the thighs up. The figure on the left is bent over, with their upper body leaning forward and their face directed downward. The individual on the left has uncovered hair and is wearing a garment with wide sleeves. The person on the right is standing upright, has a beard, is wearing headwear and a cloak draped over their shoulders. Both figures wear loose, flowing robes. The background includes trees, foliage, and a large vase or urn on the ground, indicating an outdoor setting.

artworks.title: Wooded Landscape with a Herd of Goats and a Herm
artworks.medium: etching on laid paper tinted pale blue
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with a cluster of trees at the horizon, a large tree blending into the figure of a man in the foreground, and a flock of sheep grazing in the distance. The style features detailed linework and textures resembling etching or engraving, using a monochromatic palette of black and white for depth and contrast.

artworks.title: Une répétition à L'Oeuvre, Program for L'Oasis
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper bound in theater program with blue paper cover
artworks.dimensions:
page size: 30.2 x 20.6 cm (11 7/8 x 8 1/8 in.)
overall size (program opened): 30.2 x 42.1 cm (11 7/8 x 16 9/16 in.)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theater stage during a rehearsal. The image shows an interior view of a theater, with a stage framed by a large proscenium arch. The stage is bustling with activity, as silhouettes of figures are clustered towards the center. The background features tall curtains, and stair steps lead up to the elevated stage platform. The drawing employs a sketchy, dynamic style with strong contrasts of light and shadow, giving the scene a sense of depth and motion. The intricate cross-hatching technique is used to convey texture and form, particularly in the drapery and the architectural elements of the stage.

artworks.title: La Vie muette
artworks.medium: lithograph in green-black on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring text and abstract figures in a forest setting. The composition is rustic and sepia-toned. The drawing contains text that reads "LA VIE MUETTE." On the left, there are abstract, intertwined forms resembling figures in motion, drawn with flowing lines. On the right, there is a figure standing among trees, facing away and wearing a long coat. The background shows an abstract forest scene with tree trunks. The drawing style is influenced by late 19th-century aesthetics with impressionistic outlines and textures.

artworks.title: Les Soutiens de la société
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a room with text and figures within it. The composition is divided into two parts: the left side filled with textual information about a theatrical performance and the right side illustrating a dimly lit room with several figures. The figures are sketched in an expressive, loose style, creating a slightly mysterious atmosphere. The central figure appears seated, surrounded by draped curtains, hints of a window, and indistinct forms suggesting other furniture or objects in the room. The text provides details of a publication and a performance by Henrik Ibsen. The dark, scratchy lines and shading of the drawing contribute to an overall dramatic and enigmatic mood.

artworks.title: Les Soutiens de la société
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an interior scene. The image depicts a room with a window, framed with patterned glass and partially concealed by draped curtains. Within the room, there are several indistinct figures. The overall atmosphere is intimate and somewhat somber, with heavy use of shadow and light creating depth and texture. The figures are gathered around a central point.

artworks.title: Rosmersholm
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image features a sketch-like drawing of a scene with a seated, bald figure and a standing figure to the left. Handwritten text details names and roles related to "Rosmersholm" by Henrik Ibsen. The background shows floral-like shapes and a grid pattern suggesting windows. The composition has a loose, impressionistic feel.

artworks.title: Solness le constructeur
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows a series of vertical lines and blurred shapes that create depth and movement. The composition gives the impression of tall trees in a forest. There is text overlay with titles and names, integrating with the misty background. The overall appearance is of an old, weathered poster resembling vintage playbills.

artworks.title: Un Ennemi du peuple
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image displays swirling and curving shapes and lines that contribute to its abstract quality. The text is arranged in a non-linear fashion, with curving lines that suggest a dynamic flow. Interspersed among the text are illustrated forms that hint at human figures, seen on the left and towards the bottom. The visual arrangement creates an impression of a theatrical poster with an artistic style that abstracts the concept of a playbill into a bold composition.
